newsitem.title: USA: N.Y jobless rate to lowest level in nearly 6 years.
newsitem.headline: N.Y jobless rate to lowest level in nearly 6 years.

text.p: New York State on Tuesday said that its unemployment rate dropped below six percent for the first time in nearly six years as hirings by the service sector and government increased.

The state's unemployment rate fell to 5.7 percent in September, down 0.3 percentage point from August, said the state Department of Labor. The September rate also marked an improvement from the year-ago period, when unemployment stood at 6.2 percent.

In New York City, the job outlook also brightened, as the number of unemployed people slipped below 500,000 for the first time since 1990, while the unemployment rate fell to eight percent, down from 8.5 percent in August.
However, the city also had the state's two counties with the highest unemployment rates, with the rate in the Bronx at 9.7 percent and Kings County at 8.9 percent.
The two counties in New York State with the lowest levels of unemployment were Tompkins at 3.1 percent and Yates at 3.2 percent.

Throughout the state, employment rose by 9,500 jobs in the service area, with government adding 9,000 workers. While public schools, colleges and universities added 81,300 jobs with the start of the school year, the rest of government lost 72,300 jobs as summer youth and park programs ended.
As a result, government employment was at its lowest level for the month of September since 1985.

The transportation and public utilities together added 9,000 positions. These gains far exceeded those achieved by other areas, as retail trade only added 3,000 jobs, while non-durable goods manufacturing gained 1,300. And construction jobs rose by 100.
One sector experienced sharp losses, as 5,600 jobs were shed in finance, insurance and real estate. The durable goods sector lost 500 positions.
